intended_use: A check of the method on public data with real outcomes. This model is not for scoring anyone: it shows how the same pipeline does where the outcomes are known.

metrics.measured_on: validation period; the test_ numbers are from the held-back test period, used once
metrics.split: by time (train on earlier loans, measure on later ones)
metrics.split_note: Split by loan issue date. Each period ends the day before the next begins.
metrics.model_choice: LightGBM adds -0.2377 AUC over the logistic regression (range -0.2550 to -0.2187). It is used only if the whole range reaches +0.0100 and its Brier score is not worse. Here the whole range of the gain does not reach it and its Brier score is worse, so the logistic regression stays.
metrics.inputs: The number of months over which the loan is to be repaid | 1 when the field partner, not the lender, carries the loss if the borrower does not pay
metrics.simpler_model: the loan's terms only, without the two inputs about the field partner
metrics.test_reading: On the later test months the model ranks loans the wrong way round (AUC below 0.5). This confirms that it must not be used.
metrics.data_source: Kiva loans in Asia from Kiva's snapshot of 2 May 2016 (Internet Archive copy), retail, food and services
metrics.terms: No data licence stated, only Kiva's general terms of use
metrics.label: Repaid: the loan was paid back, not defaulted
metrics.banner: Public data: Kiva (Asia), not ShopUp data. Decision support only.
metrics.what_this_shows: Where the only information is about the loan and its field partner, a score cannot be trusted.
metrics.what_this_does_not_show: Anything about scoring a merchant from behaviour. This model must not be used to pick out risky loans, and its AUC must not be quoted as support.
metrics.group_findings: Ranking differs for borrower gender 'female' (13,758 loans): AUC 0.66 against 0.51 for everyone else. Ranking differs for borrower gender 'male' (1,319 loans): AUC 0.52 against 0.66 for everyone else. Ranking differs for country 'Philippines' (10,857 loans): AUC 0.82 against 0.33 for everyone else. Ranking differs for country 'Pakistan' (605 loans): AUC 0.45 against 0.65 for everyone else. Calibration differs for country 'Pakistan' (605 loans, 79% repaid): the model expects 16 points more repayment than happened for this group, against 1 point less repayment than happened for everyone else. Ranking differs for country 'Indonesia' (253 loans): AUC 0.39 against 0.64 for everyone else. Calibration differs for country 'Indonesia' (253 loans, 84% repaid): the model expects 9 points more repayment than happened for this group, against about as much repayment as happened for everyone else.

limitations: Public data, not ShopUp data. Not usable for scoring: see 'What this does not show'.

The periods follow each other with no gap. The outcome of a loan issued near the end of one period became known only after the next period began, but training (and the calibration) used it as if it had been known. A strict forward test would leave a gap; without it the results are a little optimistic.
Labels exist only for people who received credit before. The model may not work for applicants who would have been turned down under earlier policy.
Scores are less certain when coverage is low. A thin file is never treated as a bad file: below the coverage line the band is 'Needs more info', whatever the score.
The validation numbers are a little optimistic: that period was also used to choose the model and the calibration. The held-back test period gives the honest check.
Group columns are used only to audit results, never as model inputs. The group audit shows where the model works measurably differently on these data; it does not show that the model is fair.
The tool supports a human decision. It must not be used for automatic approval or decline.
